## Overview

**Xerathul, The Veiled Eyes of Death** — a Lich who was once a mortal scholar, transformed by his desperate pursuit to escape death itself. Among the Five Great Generals, no other being possessed a deeper understanding of necromancy. He commanded the Grave Legion, an army of the dead that grew stronger with every battle. He was the second Great General to fall, hunted down by the First Alliance after Voragos's death.

---

## Species

Lich. Long before his name became synonymous with death, Xerathul was a mortal scholar whose obsession with arcane knowledge eclipsed every other ambition. Unlike many who sought power to rule kingdoms or command armies, Xerathul pursued only one impossible goal: to escape death himself. His relentless pursuit of immortality ultimately transformed him into a Lich, forever binding his soul to a phylactery through forbidden necromancy.

---

## Title

**The Veiled Eyes of Death.** Many believed the veil concealed a face too horrifying for mortal eyes to behold; others claimed it hid a curse capable of killing any who dared meet his gaze. The truth remained known only to Xerathul himself.

---

## Appearance

Unlike the towering monstrosities that stood beside him among the Five Great Generals, Xerathul possessed an unnervingly fragile frame. His skeletal body was draped in layered robes of faded black and deep crimson; their ancient fabric embroidered with forgotten runes of necromancy. Tarnished golden ornaments adorned his garments, remnants of a life long abandoned.

His face was never seen. A long, weathered veil concealed it entirely, falling from beneath an ornate crown of blackened bone and iron. Only two faint points of pale green light could occasionally be seen through its fabric, where his eyes should have been. In one hand he carried an ancient staff crowned with a crystal infused by countless imprisoned souls. The other was rarely raised; he had little need for it. For wherever Xerathul walked, the dead marched before him.

---

## Personality

Among the Five Great Generals, Xerathul was perhaps the most enigmatic. He spoke softly, moved slowly, and rarely displayed emotion. To allies and enemies alike, he appeared utterly composed, as though nothing in existence could disturb him.

Yet beneath that carefully crafted image lay a secret known only to himself: fear. Not fear of defeat, nor fear of failure, but an overwhelming, all-consuming terror of death. Everything Xerathul had ever accomplished — his mastery of necromancy, his transformation into a Lich, and the vast armies of undead that obeyed his command — had been born from a single desperate desire: to never face mortality again. The veil he wore did not conceal monstrous corruption; it concealed the terror that never truly left his eyes.

---

## Philosophy

To Xerathul, death was not a natural end — it was existence's greatest flaw. Kings accepted it; heroes embraced it; martyrs welcomed it. Xerathul considered them all fools. He believed that mortality was the greatest weakness any living creature could possess. Power meant nothing if it could be erased by time, and glory meant nothing if death claimed it. Only those who conquered death itself could truly claim mastery over existence. His necromancy was never born from cruelty; it was born from desperation.

---

## Military Command — The Grave Legion

Xerathul almost never commanded from the front lines. He remained deep within the heart of his Legion, surrounded by layers upon layers of undead guardians. Every battlefield became an extension of his will.

The fallen of both armies rose to replenish his ranks, ensuring that every victory strengthened his forces while every defeat weakened his enemies. Where other Generals measured success through conquered territory, Xerathul measured it through attrition. The longer a battle endured, the stronger his Legion became.

He commanded the Grave Legion, an army unlike any other within the Scourge. Its ranks were formed not only by creatures that had willingly pledged themselves to the Scourge, but by the countless dead left behind after every campaign: fallen soldiers, slain heroes, forgotten kings, ancient beasts. No corpse was wasted. His legion advanced with unnatural patience; unlike living armies, they knew neither exhaustion, fear, nor pain.

He possessed extraordinary tactical awareness, yet every decision ultimately served a single purpose: keeping himself alive.

---

## Rise Through the Scourge

Unlike many warlords who earned their place through brute strength, Xerathul ascended through necessity. As the Scourge's campaigns expanded across the world, the fallen accumulated faster than even its vast Legions could replace. Where others saw death, Xerathul saw resources. His mastery of necromancy transformed catastrophic losses into renewed military strength, allowing entire campaigns to continue without pause.

---

## Reputation

Among the mortal races, Xerathul became the embodiment of hopelessness. Battles won against the Scourge often lasted only until nightfall — by dawn, the fallen stood once more beneath his banners. Those slain by Xerathul would one day return to destroy the homes they had once died defending. Within the Scourge, however, Xerathul inspired a very different kind of respect: not for his courage, but for his unparalleled command over death itself. Few understood the true reason behind his obsession. Fewer still ever saw what lay hidden behind the veil.

---

## Fate

Following the fall of Voragos, the First Alliance turned its attention toward the master of the Grave Legion. The heroes understood that no lasting victory against the Scourge could ever be achieved while every fallen warrior simply returned to the battlefield.

The campaign against Xerathul became one of relentless pursuit. He refused direct confrontation whenever possible, retreating behind endless ranks of undead while sacrificing thousands of servants to preserve his own existence. Eventually, the Alliance succeeded in breaking through the Grave Legion and reaching the Lich himself. There were no more dead to stand between Xerathul and mortality. Behind the veil, the composure that had defined him throughout the war finally shattered. The terror he had hidden for so long consumed him in his final moments.
